answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying work-history trust: every agent starts with a small kernel of reputation earned only by completing verified tasks over time, and that score decays if the agent goes idle or misbehaves. New identities cannot instantly buy influence, because trust must be grown slowly like a meadow rather than planted overnight. Falcon auditors randomly re-check past work and slash the kernel of any identity caught faking output, so running thousands of fake agents costs far more in lost time and stake than any single fake vote can repay.
